newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares seen mixed, in defensive mood.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares seen mixed, in defensive mood.

text.p: Singapore stocks are seen mixed on Wednesday after initially gaining on the back of June export figures earlier this week, dealers said.
"I don't see any reason for the market to go higher," a dealer with a foreign brokerage said.
A reason for the spurt after June non-oil exports rose 8.8 percent in nominal terms year-on-year was that traders were covering back after taking short positions, he said.
On Tuesday, the Straits Times Industrials Index pared some of Monday's gains, closing down 0.24 points at 1,950.51.
Dealers said that funds were likely to continue scouring the Singapore market for bargains while retail investors may eye Malaysian property and construction stocks.

Elsewhere, Wall Street closed at a record of 8,061.65, up 154.93 points overnight after congressional testimony from Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan contained no unsettling remarks on the economy or the financial markets.
